arxiv-1610-06139.title: The complementarity relations of quantum coherence in quantum information processing
arxiv-1610-06139.creator: Fei Pan, Liang Qiu, Zhi Liu
arxiv-1610-06139.description: Abstract We establish two complementarity relations for the relative entropy of coherence in quantum information processing, i.e., quantum dense coding and teleportation. We first give an uncertainty-like expression relating local quantum coherence to the capacity of optimal dense coding for bipartite system.

arxiv-2202-04902.title: Composite Spin Approach to the Blockade Effect in Rydberg Atom Arrays
arxiv-2202-04902.creator: Lei Pan, Hui Zhai
arxiv-2202-04902.description: Abstract The Rydberg blockade induces strongly correlated many-body effects in Rydberg atom arrays, including rich ground-state phases and many-body scar states in the excitation spectrum. In this letter, we propose a composite spin representation that can provide a unified description for major features in this system.

arxiv-2210-05838.title: Pontryagin Duality for Modules over Compact Discrete Valuation Rings
arxiv-2210-05838.creator: by Milo Moses
arxiv-2210-05838.description: Abstract We establish an analogue of Pontryagin duality for modules over compact discrete valuation rings R R . Namely, we define the dual of a topological R R module to be its continuous R R -module homomorphisms into K / R K/R , the quotient module of the fraction field by its ring of integers.

arxiv-2310-10833.title: Proper Laplacian Representation Learning
arxiv-2310-10833.creator: Diego Gomez, Michael Bowling, Marlos C. MachadoDepartment of Computing Science, University of AlbertaAlberta Machine Intelligence Institute (Amii)
arxiv-2310-10833.description: Abstract The ability to learn good representations of states is essential for solving large reinforcement learning problems, where exploration, generalization, and transfer are particularly challenging. The Laplacian representation is a promising approach to address these problems by inducing informative state encoding and intrinsic rewards for temporally-extended action discovery and reward shaping.

arxiv-2505-09718.title: Neural models for prediction of spatially patterned phase transitions: methods and challenges
arxiv-2505-09718.creator: Daniel Dylewsky, Sonia Kéfi, Madhur Anand, Chris T. Bauch
arxiv-2505-09718.description: Abstract Dryland vegetation ecosystems are known to be susceptible to critical transitions between alternative stable states when subjected to external forcing. Such transitions are often discussed through the framework of bifurcation theory, but the spatial patterning of vegetation, which is characteristic of drylands, leads to dynamics that are much more complex and diverse than local bifurcations.

arxiv-2506-12128.title: Improved Ground State Estimation in Quantum Field Theories via Normalising Flow-Assisted Neural Quantum States
arxiv-2506-12128.creator: Vishal S. Ngairangbam, Michael Spannowsky, Timur Sypchenko
arxiv-2506-12128.description: Abstract We propose a hybrid variational framework that enhances Neural Quantum States (NQS) with a Normalising Flow-based sampler to improve the expressivity and trainability of quantum many-body wavefunctions. Our approach decouples the sampling task from the variational ansatz by learning a continuous flow model that targets a discretised, amplitude-supported subspace of the Hilbert space.

arxiv-2510-08711.title: In-Context Learning for Non-Stationary MIMO Equalization
arxiv-2510-08711.creator: Jiachen Jiang, Zhen Qin, Zhihui Zhu
arxiv-2510-08711.description: Abstract Channel equalization is fundamental for mitigating distortions such as frequency-selective fading and inter-symbol interference. Unlike standard supervised learning approaches that require costly retraining or fine-tuning for each new task, in-context learning (ICL) adapts to new channels at inference time with only a few examples.

pmc-10541696.title: Implication of red meat consumption habits in serum uric acid levels and mood disorders among first-trimester pregnant women
pmc-10541696.creator: Mudi H Alharbi, Nora HJ Alharbi, Ibtihal A Brnawi, Elham H Atiq
pmc-10541696.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). BackgroundDietary pattern involving meat consumption has an association with serum uric acid level which subsequently has an impact on moods. However, this relationship is not clearly established in pregnant women, particularly those who are accustomed to daily meat consumption.ObjectiveThis study investigated the relationship between red meat consumption and uric acid level and the subsequent impact on mood disorders in 1st trimester pregnant women.MethodologyA total of 92 pregnant women in their first trimester (8–12 weeks), were selected for this study.

pmc-11334453.title: Determining lactate concentrations in Korean indigenous calves and evaluating its role as a predictor for acidemia in calf diarrhea
pmc-11334453.creator: Youngwoo Jung, Ji-Yeong Ku, Byoungsoo Kim, Youngjun Kim, Kwang-Man Park, Jonghun Baek, DoHyeon Yu, Jinho Park
pmc-11334453.description: BackgroundCalf diarrhea leads to high mortality rates and decreases in growth and productivity, causing negative effects on the livestock industry. Lactate is closely associated with metabolic acidosis in diarrheic calves. However, there have been no reports on lactate concentrations in Korean indigenous (Hanwoo) calves, especially those with diarrhea.

pmc-11419314.title: A case report of a colouterine fistula due to sigmoid diverticulitis
pmc-11419314.creator: Catherine L A Chang, Kenley R Unruh, Chad E Cragle, Ravi Moonka
pmc-11419314.description: Colouterine fistulas are generally seen in post-menopausal patients and present with abdominal pain and non-physiologic vaginal drainage. A history of uterine pathology or diverticulitis is generally lacking. Visualization of the passage of contrast from the gastrointestinal tract to the uterus is not necessary to make the diagnosis.

pmc-11463993.title: Advancing insights in critical COVID-19: unraveling lymphopenia through propensity score matching - Findings from the Multicenter LYMPH-COVID Study
pmc-11463993.creator: José Pedro Cidade, Vicente Cês Souza-Dantas, Rafaela Braga Mamfrim, Renata Carnevale Miranda, Henrique Tommasi Caroli, Natália Almeida Oliveira, Alessandra e Figueiredo Thompson, Gabriela E. Oliveira, Pedro Póvoa, José Pedro Cidade, Vicente Cês Souza-Dantas, Rafaela Braga Mamfrim, Renata Carnevale M
pmc-11463993.description: Objective To elucidate the impact of lymphopenia on critical COVID-19 patient outcomes.Methods We conducted a multicenter prospective cohort study across five hospitals in Portugal and Brazil from 2020 to 2021. The study included adult patients admitted to the intensive care unit with SARS-CoV-2 pneumonia.

pmc-11488125.title: Measuring the crowding of emergency departments: an assessment of the NEDOCS in Lombardy, Italy, and the development of a new objective indicator based on the waiting time for the first clinical assessment
pmc-11488125.creator: Fabiola Signorini, Giovanni Nattino, Carlotta Rossi, Walter Ageno, Felice Catania, Francesca Cortellaro, Giorgio Costantino, Andrea Duca, Giulia Irene Ghilardi, Stefano Paglia, Paolo Pausilli, Cristiano Perani, Giuseppe Sechi, Guido Bertolini
pmc-11488125.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundThere is no ubiquitous definition of Emergency Department (ED) crowding and several indicators have been proposed to measure it. The National ED Overcrowding Study (NEDOCS) score is among the most popular, even though it has been severely criticised.

pmc-11503651.title: Genetic Code Expansion Approaches to Decipher the Ubiquitin Code
pmc-11503651.creator: Vera Wanka, Maximilian Fottner, Marko Cigler, Kathrin Lang
pmc-11503651.description: The covalent attachment of Ub (ubiquitin) to target proteins (ubiquitylation) represents one of the most versatile PTMs (post-translational modifications) in eukaryotic cells. Substrate modifications range from a single Ub moiety being attached to a target protein to complex Ub chains that can also contain Ubls (Ub-like proteins).

pmc-12427929.title: Natural Killer Cell Therapy Combined with Probiotic Bacteria Supplementation Restores Bone Integrity in Cancer by Promoting IFN-γ Production
pmc-12427929.creator: Kawaljit Kaur, Patricia Reese, Jason Chiang, Anahid Jewett, Alessandro Poggi
pmc-12427929.description: Simple SummaryThe study explored the complex link between the immune system and bone structure, emphasizing the key role of IFN-γ in preserving skeletal integrity. Targeting the IFN-γ signaling pathway offers a promising way to strengthen bones and tackle cancer-induced bone disorders.

pmc-12550627.title: Regioselective Electrochemical Borylation of Oxygenated Allylic Electrophiles: Method Development and Synthetic Applications
pmc-12550627.creator: Wan-Chen Cindy Lee, Pierre-Louis Lagueux-Tremblay, Zongbin Jia, Song Lin
pmc-12550627.description: Allylboronic esters are highly versatile intermediates in organic synthesis. In this work, we report a general and scalable strategy for the regioselective deoxygenative borylation of allylic alcohols, enals, enones, and acrylates, upgrading these abundant functional groups in feedstock chemicals and natural products into value-added borylated synthetic handles.

pmc-13079769.title: Association of surgical resection with survival in retroperitoneal leiomyosarcoma based on SEER propensity score matching and machine-learning models
pmc-13079769.creator: Kun Huang, Zhenghong Huang, Yunshen He, Pan Zhao, Xiaofeng Hu
pmc-13079769.description: Retroperitoneal leiomyosarcoma (RLS) is a rare and aggressive subtype of soft tissue sarcoma with limited population-level evidence guiding surgical decision-making. This study aimed to assess the prognostic value of surgery in patients with RLS using a large real-world cohort and advanced analytical methods.

pmc-13279877.title: Correction to “Political Ideology and HPV Vaccine Awareness: Sex Differences and Nursing Implications Using the Health Information National Trends Survey (HINTS)”

pmc-13603133.title: From Oscillations to Brain States: Real-Time EEG-TMS for Adaptive Neuromodulation
pmc-13603133.creator: Melissa Null, Elena Mongiardini, Chiara Leu, Giulia Liberati, Paolo Belardinelli
pmc-13603133.description: Transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) enables non-invasive, focal modulation of cortical circuits by inducing electric currents in the brain through electromagnetic induction, thereby influencing neuronal excitability and synaptic plasticity. High inter- and intra-individual variability has led, however, to moderate efficacy and reproducibility of stimulation and treatment protocols, motivating a shift toward brain-state-dependent stimulation.

pmc-13613929.title: Occurrence Patterns and Controlling Mechanisms of In Situ Gas Content in Varied Marine Siliceous Shale Subfacies: A Case Study of the Wufeng–Longmaxi Formation in the Anchang Syncline, Northern Guizhou, China
pmc-13613929.creator: Ming Xie, Shaobin Guo, Jiliang Yu, Deqiang Sun, Hailong Li, Gangquan Li, Xinbing He
pmc-13613929.description: Significant discrepancies in in situ gas content and occurrence characteristics exist among different siliceous shale subfacies of the Wufeng–Longmaxi Formation, yet the underlying controlling mechanisms remain poorly understood, particularly in normal-pressure shale gas reservoirs. This study systematically investigated the gas-bearing heterogeneity and its dominant controls in the Anchang syncline, a representative normal-pressure block in northern Guizhou.

pmc-13672432.title: Frailty, physiological reserve, and surgical resilience: toward a dynamic stress–recovery model
pmc-13672432.creator: Rafal Cudnik, Mirko Barone, Luigi Marano, Simone Gargarella, Ruslan Duka, Robert Molchanov, Sergii Girnyi, Tomasz Cwalinski, Mahmoud Al-Balas, Yogesh Vashist, Lorenzo Cobianchi, Silvia Malerba, Francesco Paolo Prete, Mario Testini, Valentin Calu, Archil Aladashvili, Kamal Mahawar, Arda Isik, Virgini
pmc-13672432.description: BackgroundChronological age remains widely used in perioperative decision-making but incompletely captures the biological heterogeneity that influences postoperative outcomes. Frailty has substantially advanced surgical risk assessment by shifting attention from age toward multidimensional vulnerability and diminished physiological reserve. Nevertheless, patients with similar frailty profiles often experience markedly different recovery trajectories, suggesting that baseline vulnerability alone may not fully explain postoperative adaptation.
